column4: Visit note | 2025-04-20 02:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Rakib Rahman, 75, male. Mr. Rahman reports that he feels nausea with the spinning, experiences brief spinning when turning in bed, and has dizziness when looking up. He mentions that these symptoms began after a viral cold in Tongi. He works as a farmer, is married, and does not smoke. He has Bronchial asthma. He denies headaches, weakness, or hearing loss. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the left side, BP 112/79 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 53 kg. Cranial nerves are intact and gait is steady when not dizzy. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-04-20 04:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Masud Howlader, 37, male. Mr. Howlader attends for a review of his ongoing headaches and reports frequent nausea and needing to lie in a dark room. He works as a bus driver and notes that his symptoms are worse since bright screens at a new job in Bogura. He takes his preventive regimen as instructed and has noticed some mild fluctuations in frequency, logging about 7 headache days a month recently. He has Bronchial asthma, which remains stable without recent exacerbations. He denies any visual changes, numbness, or weakness during attacks. On physical and neurological examinations today: BP 120/86 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm, weight 58 kg. Fundoscopy is normal, visual fields are full, and coordination tests are intact. Assessment: Migraine. Plan: a prescription was issued to adjust his prophylactic therapy. He was advised to keep a headache diary, sleep and eat at regular times, and limit screen time. Follow-up in 3 months with the headache diary.
